sentences.text:
The petitioner is before this Court seeking for the following reliefs:
i. Call for the records in CC. No.26092/2016 (PCR No.4944/2016) on the file of the 4th Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, at Bangalore.
ii.

entities.text: 4th Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, at Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Allow the petition and quash the order dated 21.09.2016 passed in CC.No.26092/2016 on the file of the 4th Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Bangalore and the Investigation report and entire proceedings in CC.No.26092/2016 filed against the petitioner/accused no.54 for the alleged offences punishable under section 406 and 120B of IPC.
iii. Pass such other orders as this Hon'ble Court deems fit in the circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice.
2. The respondent - Serious Fraud Investigation officer has filed a private complaint in PCR No.4944/2016 before IV Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore against 54 persons where the petitioner was arrayed as accused No.54 alleging that there were violations of Section 621 of Companies Act, 1956, Sections 58-A, 150, 151, 152, 159, 161, 193, 209, 210, 303, NC:
2024:KHC:10421 307, 372A, 240, 628, 629 of the Companies Act, 1956 and Sections 177, 181, 403,
405, 406, 409, 420, 379, 381 and 120B of IPC.
The investigation report indicates that the charges alleged against the petitioner are under Section 406 read with Section 120B of IPC.
It is challenging the same that the petitioner is before this Court seeking for the aforesaid reliefs.

3. Sri.Manjunath G.Kandekar, learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner - accused No.54 was engaged by the officers of the accused No.1 to make gold coins out of gold purchased by the company and/or its officers, which has been so done by the petitioner.

2 petitioner is in no manner concerned with any of the criminal offences committed by the other accused.

entities.text: Mr. P Ravichandran vs Serious Fraud Investigation Office
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Though there is interaction between the officers of accused No.1 with the petitioner, the petitioner was only involved in making available then prevalent gold prices after NC:
2024:KHC:10421 verification of the same from the Bhima Jewelers and making them known to the said officers.
Collecting the gold bar from officers of accused No.1 or Bhima Jewelers for making gold coins and handing over to the respective officers.
Apart there from, the petitioner is not concerned with any of the actions taken by the other accused.
The petitioner was not involved and/or is not party to any of the criminal offences.
On the above grounds, he seeks for quashing of the proceedings by allowing the Criminal Petition insofar as petitioner is concerned.
4. Sri.

Venkataramana, learned counsel for the respondent would however submit that there are various allegations made against the petitioner inasmuch as gold was handed over to the petitioner,
thereafter, the petitioner would make the gold coins.
The total gold purchased by the company was 141.65 kgs whereas the gold coins which have been prepared by the petitioner - accused No.54 is 37.58 NC: 2024:KHC:10421 kgs.
The balance of the gold has not been accounted for.
The petitioner playing the actual part in receiving the gold and making of the gold coins is guilty of offences which have been alleged including Section 406 read with Section 120B of IPC.
On the above grounds, he submits that the petition is required to be dismissed.

5. Heard Sri.Manjunath G.Kandekar, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.Venkataramana,
learned counsel for the respondent and perused the papers.
6.
Section 406 of IPC provides for offence under Section 405 of IPC.

Section 405 and 406 of IPC reads as under:-
405. Criminal breach of trust.--Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, or of any legal contract, express or implied, which he has made touching the discharge of such trust, or wilfully suffers any other person so to do, commits "criminal breach of trust".

Explanation 1.--A person, being an employer of an establishment whether exempted under section 17 of the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions NC: 2024:KHC:10421 Act, 1952 (19 of 1952) or not] who deducts the employee's contribution from the wages payable to the employee for credit to a Provident Fund or Family Pension Fund established by any law for the time being in force, shall be deemed to have been entrusted with the amount of the contribution so deducted by him and if he makes default in the payment of such contribution to the said Fund in violation of the said law, shall be deemed to have dishonestly used the amount of the said contribution in violation of a direction of law as aforesaid. Explanation 2.--A person, being an employer, who deducts the employees' contribution from the wages payable to the employee for credit to the Employees' State Insurance Fund held and administered by the Employees' State Insurance Corporation established under the Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 (34 of 1948),

3 shall be deemed to have been entrusted with the amount of the contribution so deducted by him and if he makes default in the payment of such contribution to the said Fund in violation of the said Act,
shall be deemed to have dishonestly used the amount of the said contribution in violation of a direction of law as aforesaid.

sentences.text: 406. Punishment for criminal breach of trust.-- Whoever commits criminal breach of trust shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

7. The only allegation which has been made against the petitioner is that the petitioner has prepared gold coins out of gold supplied by accused No.1 and its officers, which has been used by accused No.1 and its officers in a ponzi scheme.

There are no allegations which have been made against the NC:
2024:KHC:10421 petitioner insofar as Scheme is concerned or in any of the offences relating thereto.

The only allegation being for a preparation of gold coins, I am of the considered opinion that offences under Section 405 of IPC would not be attracted since the petitioner has not misappropriated or converted any property for his own use.
8. The petitioner, having been provided with gold bars by the officers of accused No.1 he has made the gold coins and returned it to the officers.
There being no allegation against the petitioner regarding retaining any gold with himself and/or making use of any gold for his own benefit.

The allegations against the accused No.1 and officers of accused No.1 are that by making use of the monies received from unsuspecting persons has been used by the accused and that cannot be attributed to the petitioner - accused No.54 who is only involved in making gold coins.
In that view of the matter, I do not find any of the ingredients of Section 405 IPC being satisfied in the present matter requiring punishment under Section 406 of IPC.

Hence, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The Criminal Petition is allowed.
ii) The proceedings in C.C.No.26092/2016 (PCR No.4944/2016) pending before 4th Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bangalore insofar as the petitioner - accused No.54 is concerned is quashed.
iii) It is made clear that this Court has not expressed any opinion as regards involvement or otherwise of other accused.
